renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: orthogroup_upset
  title: Orthogroups shared between species
  description: |-
    Each bar is a set of species and counts the orthogroups that contain genes from exactly those species, with the dots below naming the set. It answers which orthogroups every species shares, which a clade shares and which belong to a single species.
    How to read: the bar with every species joined is the core set that all genomes carry. Tall bars for a subset of species point to a clade-specific gene family, and a species with a large single bar holds many genes found nowhere else, which is also what a fragmented or contaminated proteome looks like.
    Lines and annotations: bars are coloured by the number of species in the set, the degree of the intersection.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree
    show_values: true

- component: card
  id: orthogroups_total
  title: Orthogroups
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of orthogroups, the bar splits them by copy class, and the strip gives the median and largest number of genes in an orthogroup. It answers how many gene families the species form and how many are single copy.
    How to read: a large single-copy share means few duplications, which suits a species tree. A large multi-copy share points to expanded families.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md
  column: total_genes
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: copy_class
  caption: orthogroups, by copy class

- component: card
  title: Species per orthogroup
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average count of species that hold genes of an orthogroup, and the box shows the spread. It answers how widely shared the gene families are.
    How to read: an average close to the number of species means most families are shared by all of them. A low average with a long tail points to many species-specific families.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md
  column: n_genomes
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Copy class
  description: Filters the tiles to orthogroups of one or more copy classes, such as single copy or multi
    copy.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: copy_class

- component: table
  title: Orthogroup table
  description: |-
    Each row is an orthogroup, with a 0 or 1 column per species, the number of species it reaches, its total genes, its copy class and how widely it is shared. It answers which families make up each bar of the intersection plot.
    How to read: sort by total genes to find the largest families, or filter by sharing to list the core ones.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: one_to_one_heatmap
  title: One-to-one orthologues between species
  description: |-
    Each cell is a pair of species and gives the number of one-to-one orthologues OrthoFinder found between them, with rows and columns ordered by similarity. It answers which genomes share the most single-copy gene pairs.
    How to read: close, well annotated genomes form bright blocks. A species whose whole row is dimmer than the others has lost or split gene models, or sits far from the rest in the tree, so check its assigned share on the species tile.
    Note: the diagonal is empty, since a species has no orthologues with itself.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: genome

- component: table
  title: One-to-one orthologue counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a species and each column another species, with the count of one-to-one orthologues between the two. It answers the exact numbers behind the heatmap.
    How to read: read across a row to compare one species with every other.

- component: card
  id: assigned_share
  title: Genes placed in orthogroups
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest percentage of a species' genes that OrthoFinder placed in an orthogroup, and the box shows how the species spread. It answers whether every proteome is well represented in the orthogroups.
    How to read: values close to 100 percent mean nearly every gene has a relative. A species well below the others carries unassigned genes, and the OrthoFinder tutorial names poor species sampling around it as the most likely cause.
    Note: the tutorial likes to see at least 80 percent of all genes assigned, a guide for the run as a whole rather than a pass mark per species, so no line is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md and https://davidemms.github.io/orthofinder_tutorials/exploring-orthofinders-results.html
  column: genes_in_orthogroups_pct
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: lowest species, with the spread

- component: card
  id: species_specific
  title: Species-specific orthogroups
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of orthogroups made entirely of genes from one species, with the median and the largest count among species. It answers how much of the gene content is unique to a single genome.
    How to read: a species far above the median holds many families found nowhere else, which is real novelty or contamination and fragmentation. Open the table to see which species it is.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md
  column: species_specific_orthogroups
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: total, with the median and largest species

- component: figure
  title: Genes placed in orthogroups per species
  description: |-
    Each bar is a species, with the percentage of its genes that OrthoFinder placed in an orthogroup. It answers which proteomes are least covered by the orthogroups.
    How to read: bars of similar height mean the species are equally well covered. A short bar points to unassigned genes, which the OrthoFinder tutorial puts down mostly to poor species sampling, so compare it with the unassigned share in the table.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median share of genes in orthogroups of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of OrthoFinder.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidemms/OrthoFinder/master/README.md and https://davidemms.github.io/orthofinder_tutorials/exploring-orthofinders-results.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: genome
    y: genes_in_orthogroups_pct
    labels:
      genome: Species
      genes_in_orthogroups_pct: Genes in orthogroups (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: genes_in_orthogroups_pct

- component: table
  title: Per-species statistics
  description: |-
    Each row is a species with the genes in its proteome, the share and number placed in orthogroups, the unassigned genes, the orthogroups it takes part in and the ones it holds alone. It answers the exact numbers behind each tile.
    How to read: sort by unassigned share to find the proteomes to inspect first.
